confirmatory.hypothesis: Species turnover creates community-level spatial continuity beyond the best individual species.
confirmatory.key_observation: At every fresh site, at least one individual species survived every distinct canonical world.

ecological_result.main_statement: Community-level small-mammal continuity was inherited from individually continuous species rather than generated by species turnover.

posthoc_mechanism.interpretation: Richer sites contained more independently continuous species rather than showing stronger heterospecific rescue. This pattern is consistent with spatial continuity redundancy, not turnover-generated connectivity.

supported: The preregistered turnover-generated connectivity hypothesis failed in 16 of 16 fresh-site null-adjusted comparisons.
Individual-species sufficiency was universal across the fresh denominator.
Taxonomic pooling did not increase world survival at any site.
Community pooling can reduce continuity under an all-positive support rule, as observed at ORNL.
Exploratorily, richer sites contained more species that were each individually sufficient for complete world survival.
not_supported: Species turnover is unimportant for all aspects of metacommunity dynamics.
The best world-survival species is necessarily the numerically dominant species.
The exploratory richness-redundancy association is causal.
The result estimates dispersal rates or movement mechanisms.
The consumed programme may be retuned or expanded to improve support.
